findings.claim: The supplied continuous contrast functions are observed-node linear fits over the complete observed window [0.0,0.5]; no polynomial is accepted and extrapolation is disallowed for any of the read features, so time-conditioned rules must be restricted to the observed support.

Several landmark local contrast features show multiple sign changes and strong sign conflicts within the window (e.g. landmark_00_local_dz has 10 sign changes and 7 strong sign conflicts; landmark_00_local_dx has 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts), so a constant-sign rule is not supported for those coordinates and a time-conditioned rule is only defensible where fits are validated.

First-to-last rate reversals are present: landmark_00_soft_mass has first_rate_z positive and last_rate_z negative, while landmark_00_local_dx and landmark_00_local_dy reverse from negative first rates to positive last rates, indicating the direction of change is not stationary across the observed window.

Whole-window z values for the read features are small relative to the endpoint rate z magnitudes, so the net window-level contrast is weak even where local rates are large; whole-window summaries should not be read as absolute geometric targets.

The declared objective is final predicted target affinity primary with validity and strain secondary under coordinate-only control, and the clock metadata confirms recorded affinities were removed with an equal score prior, so no absolute affinity benefit can be claimed from these coordinate contrasts alone.

hypotheses.falsifier: a constant-sign rule matches the observed-node contrast values at least as well as the time-conditioned rule on held-out observed nodes
hypotheses.observable: observed-node contrast values of the named landmark local features across the observed score times
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned coordinate contrast rule restricted to the observed window [0.0,0.5] will track the observed sign reversals of landmark local contrast features better than a constant-sign rule, without extrapolation.

hypotheses.falsifier: rate reversal disappears when recomputed on independent batches or is explained by changing cohort composition
hypotheses.observable: first_rate_z and last_rate_z of the named features
hypotheses.statement: The first-to-last rate reversals in landmark_00_soft_mass and landmark_00_local_dx/dy reflect within-window change in the contrast function rather than a stable cohort-level shift.

limitations: Only the first six continuous_trends rows were read; the remaining 194 features were not inspected, so the findings are not exhaustive over the 200 registered curve features.
No decoded terminal labels or outcome evaluation data were supplied, so last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.
Turnover accounting, increment effects, joint diagnostics and lineage support tables were not read in this turn; parent-child increment versus cohort-composition attribution remains unassessed.
Contrast curves are coordinate contrasts, not absolute reward targets or physical interaction energies.
